items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: You see on piano we had Louis Russell on piano

ctx.x: Well I'll give you a few of them. You see on piano we had Louis Russell on piano, and banjo, Willie Foster, that's Pop Foster's brother, on banjo. On drums we had Paul Barbaran on drums. And on bass we had a bass player called Buford. Now on trumpet we had King Oliver, Red Island, so far back I can't think of the boy's name. Yeah. That's what I remember. Boy, he just died too, not so long ago.
Great kind of guy. Darnell Harris?

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: And we had Kid O'Reilly on trombone, but Louis Russell did all of that.

ctx.x: Was he doing a range here in the band? Was he doing a range here?

Yeah, he'd do some range, he was doing a range. And we had Kid O'Reilly on trombone, but Louis Russell did all of that. After that band broke up, we went on the road. We had trombone played, they did all the business. Pete, I can't think of his name unless I look up the name.
I think I have it outside in the car. Yeah. I didn't want to get it if you wanted to.

items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: No, I recorded, it's a record I recorded with Louis Russell's band.

ctx.x: That's when Barney went with him.

And yeah, Barney Big Odd went with him. And Duke Ellington was looking for me for saxophone, but he couldn't find me. So instead of getting me he got Johnny Hodges. Now Simeon left and he went to Milwaukee and then back he joined Earl Hines band. So Louis Russ, I was around doing anything. I was playing around with different bands, a fellow called Wilkins, a piano player, and Edgar Dow, a piano player, Jinger Young, Richard Cheatham from Cleveland, Ohio. I played a gig with Chick Webb's band. You know, a…
I believe I heard it, Dave Nelson.
